targets.outcome_quote:
In conclusion, as in Part I of the present study, we could replicate the seminal work
by Langer and Roth (1975), showing that the emphasis of success at the beginning of a
run enhances participants’ estimation of their ability to predict outcomes of a coin toss.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly conclude they replicated the original effect. Its small size and short duration do not override that verdict.

reasoning: Identity verified against repository title, DOI and all four authors; accepted manuscript contains full article, references and appendices. Langer and Roth 1975 is explicitly re-tested in both current experiments, independently of the separate Part I article. For post-loss speeding, Eben et al. 2020 is the nearest prior replication in the chain, rather than separately duplicating Verbruggen et al. 2017 for the same finding. Other cited works motivate theoretical predictions or provide background, not additional independently identified replication targets. The novel influence of illusory control on speeding fails, but that is not a failure of either explicitly replicated original effect.
